summary.text: Lou Correa is the Democratic incumbent in the 46th District, which covers Orange County cities including Anaheim and Santa Ana, and has served in the U.S. House since he was elected in 2016.

Before Congress he held office in the California State Assembly, on the Orange County Board of Supervisors and in the California State Senate; his campaign website describes him as the son of working-class parents who has served Orange County since 1998.

paragraphs.text: Correa grew up in Anaheim, where his mother cleaned hotel rooms across from Disneyland and his father worked at a paper mill, and he attended Benjamin Franklin Elementary, Fremont Junior High and Anaheim High School.
He earned a B.A. in economics from California State University, Fullerton in 1980, and an MBA and Juris Doctor from UCLA in 1985.
He worked as a teacher in the Rancho Santiago Community College District and as an investment banker, attorney and licensed real estate broker.
Correa lost a 1996 race for the California State Assembly and won the seat when he ran again in 1998, serving in the Assembly from 1998 to 2004.
He then sat on the Orange County Board of Supervisors from 2004 to 2006 and in the California State Senate from 2006 to 2014, winning the 34th District seat in 2006 and re-election in 2010.

Correa won the 46th District seat in 2016 after Rep. Loretta Sanchez left it to run for U.S. Senate; he finished first in the June top-two primary and defeated fellow Democrat Bao Nguyen in the general election with 70% of the vote.
For 2025 and 2026 he is assigned to the House Homeland Security Committee, including its Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee, and to the Judiciary Committee.
Correa lives in Santa Ana with his wife, Esther, and their four children, and is a member of Christ Cathedral Catholic Church, according to his official biography.
